targets.authors: Nicholls, M. E. R., Churches, O. & Loetscher, T.
targets.title: Perception of an ambiguous figure is affected by own-age social biases.
targets.evidence_quote: We present a study that aims to examine whether the findings by Nicholls et al. can be best explained by the own-age social group bias or the own-age anchor effect. In order to do this, we will replicate the original study as closely as possible, but in addition ask participants to indicate whether they saw the young woman or the older lady.
targets.outcome_quote: Our results disqualify the original finding as an example of cognitive penetrability: the participants’ age biases their judgment of the ambiguous figure, not its perception.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The age-estimate effect replicates, but the main conclusion is that the original measure cannot establish the claimed perceptual bias.

reasoning: New participants repeat the published Nicholls et al. experiment; the central message challenges the validity of the original inference despite recovering its effect.
